The mission should have given us the core functionality we need based on the paper, but we haven't built demos of all of that.  Since I'm getting a little bit tired of interactive testing, I'd also like to see if we ever built the "dramaturge" feature (Playwright for Emacs)... which presumably would just be a light skin over Emacsclient.  Anyway if we can spec out a range of interactive features that would make 象-2000 "interactionally compliant" with Elephant-2000 that would be great, and then we could set about getting a kimi agent to build and test them.  I have additional ideas about what I want to do with the session but let's get the interactive feature list specified first

reply_text:
Found the dramaturge (futon4, May 2026). Now matching the mission's built packets against McCarthy's requirements, to see which have no demo.Gist: The feature list is written: `holes/labs/M-象-2000/INTERACT-1-interactional-compliance.md` (futon3c 63e44b6e). It has 13 interactive features (I1 to I13), each tied to one of McCarthy's requirements. Each is accepted by a scripted Emacs test that plants the bad case it's named for. The dramaturge exists but only checks what screens show; it can't type or press keys, so extending it to drive them is item zero and goes first. Please read the list before anything goes to Kimi. I7 and I8 also need your decision on two new record types.

**The dramaturge:** `futon4/dev/arxana-dramaturge.el`, May 2026, 528 lines. It has a test registry, assertions about buffer contents, a wait-until helper and a runner. What §0 adds:
- **A separate Emacs:** tests run in their own Emacs daemon, never yours. Tonight's window takeover happened while I was testing in your Emacs.
- **Driving:** steps that type text and press keys through the real keymaps. That would have caught the r/R bug.
- **A stand-in agent:** it replays recorded answers, so tests cost no tokens. One live check per feature runs against a real Kimi seat.
- **Results:** you run one command and read a report plus saved buffer snapshots.

**How the list was put together:** most of the mission's core is built, but as records and queries that an agent runs. It counted as met because the acceptance was about the stores. So each feature makes an existing record appear where you are working, in the REPL or the stepper, when you do the act. The main ones:

| Item | Feature |
|---|---|
| I1 | The owed/owing ledger in the REPL and at a stepper frame |
| I2 | Promise outcomes |
| I3 | Who authorised each act, shown in the stepper |
| I6 | Clickable assumptions you can reject |
| I9 | Standing rules checked on every new event (the elephantKanren loop) |
| I10 | Which rules were in force at a frame |
| I11 | An "as of this frame" view |
| I13 | Tonight's checks running live and showing up in 象's modeline indicator |

**Suggested order for Kimi:** §0 first, then I13 and I11. Those two build on tonight's code, so they're also a check that the driver works.

**Deferred, with written re-arm conditions** (following the pattern card on this turn):
- **Session-fork rewind:** your decision tonight. It's in the file with what I tested and when to reconsider it.
- **I5's provisional withdrawals:** your earlier item 17.4.

The mission file now links to the list.

**Source:** I worked from the mission's existing translation of the paper (DERIVE-1, with line references to `elephant.tex`). I didn't re-read the paper itself.
